title: Number of Islands
statement_short: Given an m x n 2D binary grid grid which represents a map of '1's (land) and '0's (water), return the number of islands. An island is surrounded by water and is formed by connecting adjacent lands horizontally or vertically.
constraints: m == grid.length, n == grid[i].length, 1 <= m, n <= 300, grid[i][j] is '0' or '1'
hint: Grid size up to 300x300 permits O(m \* n) traversal, sinking visited land cells using BFS/DFS.
keywords: connecting adjacent lands horizontally or vertically
why_not: Right: Graph BFS traverses connected land cells level by level using a queue, mutating visited cells to '0' in O(m \* n) time and O(min(m, n)) space. Not Graph DFS: DFS using recursion also sinks islands in O(m \* n) time, but risks stack overflow on deep grid components without iterative stack. Not Union-Find: Disjoint sets track connected land components in O(m \* n \* alpha(m\*n)) time, which adds auxiliary parent array memory. Not 2D DP: Dynamic programming requires directional subproblem ordering, failing for arbitrary 4-directional connected components.
complexity: O(m \* n) time, O(min(m, n)) space
